description: Which ERCOT transmission constraints bind near a site and how often, with SCED (real-time) and DAM (day-ahead) shadow prices. A binding constraint means a transmission line or transformer is at its limit, trapping cheaper energy behind it and splitting prices across the constraint. High shadow prices at a substation mean congestion creates local price extremes: good for a battery that can capture the spread, risky for a generator that might be curtailed. Shows the constraint name, overloaded element (from/to stations, voltage), contingency, how many 5-minute SCED intervals and DAM hours it bound in the window, and the average and maximum shadow price. Cross-reference with volatile_nodes to understand WHY a node is volatile (congestion versus load/supply fundamentals) and with grid_projects to see whether a planned upgrade will relieve a binding constraint. Use when someone asks why prices spike at a node, what congestion looks like near a site, whether a spread will persist, or what constraints affect a substation.

address.description: Texas street address, e.g. '1201 Main St, Houston, TX'. Use this or lat/lng.

days.description: Window in days. Default 30. Max 30 free, 120 Pro.

lat.description: Latitude (WGS84). Use with lng instead of address.

lng.description: Longitude (WGS84). Use with lat instead of address.

radius_mi.description: Radius around the location in miles. Default 25, max 100.

settlement_point.description: ERCOT settlement point name (e.g. HB_WEST or BRUNI_RN) instead of lat/lng.

name: binding_constraints
title: Transmission constraints and shadow prices near a site
